extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of political theory, public policy makers, and informed general readers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts normative criteria and practical standards about public opinion, liberalism, centralization, and the role of publics vs. actors in democratic life as set out in a political-theory text. Useful for evaluating how publics, officials, and institutions should behave and be judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of withholding facts for necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: When a statesman tells me that it is not safe for him to disclose all the facts, I am content to trust him in this if I trust him at all. There is nothing misleading in a frank refusal to tell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish a candid refusal to disclose for safety/necessity from deception. The real harm arises not from withholding per se but from pretending that everything has been disclosed. Trust is conditional on frankness; secrecy must be admitted honestly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the pretense of universal disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The mischief comes in the pretense that all is being told, that the public is entirely in the confidence of the public man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials and public actors should not claim full transparency if they are withholding information. Such pretense exploits the sophistry that public and all individuals composing it are one mind, creating false expectations and undermining trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject personification/monistic theory of society
rubrics_metrics.description: The sophistry that the public and all the individuals composing it are one mind, one soul, one purpose is an absurd sophistry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conceptualize society as relations and adjustments among individuals rather than as a single organic actor. This clears logical confusion about how many separate individuals with differing purposes can be united and avoids attributing a single collective will where none exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat society as adjustments between individuals (anti-personification)
rubrics_metrics.description: We can say without theoretical qualms what common sense plainly tells us is so: it is the individuals who act, not society; it is the individuals who think, not the collective mind ... It is their relations with each other that constitute a society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and analysis should focus on concrete relations and actors (painters, soldiers, merchants) rather than vague collective entities; publics are formed by those indirectly concerned who may align with actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political philosophies must address specific agents
rubrics_metrics.description: The great state builders ... each had in mind somebody, some group of real people, who were to realize his program. The agents in the theory have varied ... The theories are always, except in the liberal philosophy, addressed to somebody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative theories or reforms should specify who will act (landlords, peasants, unions, manufacturers, church, ruling classes) and not appeal only to abstract 'man' or 'mankind'. Practical guidance requires naming agents and mechanisms for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberalism's insufficiency: appeals must be actionable
rubrics_metrics.description: The liberal discovered a method of proving that men are finite ... but in attempting to escape to universal appeals it could not tell particular men how to behave sincerely, and so furnished them with an excellent masquerade when they behaved arbitrarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations of political philosophies should ask whether they provide concrete guidance for particular actors. Vague appeals to universal ideals may awaken sentiment but fail to instruct or constrain behavior, enabling opportunism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid addressing 'all mankind'—target the relevant public
rubrics_metrics.description: The liberal assumed that all mankind was within hearing, that all mankind when it heard would respond homogeneously ... His appeal to this cosmopolitan, universal, disinterested intuition in everybody was equivalent to an appeal to nobody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persuasion and reform should be tailored to the actual audience (those indirectly concerned who can align with an actor), not to an imagined universal public; effective appeals name and address likely allies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value pluralism: define separate functions to reduce anarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: There is least anarchy precisely in those areas of society where separate functions are most clearly defined and brought into orderly adjustment; there is most anarchy in those twilight zones ... where separateness of purpose is covered up and confused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional design and public judgment should favor clear definition of roles/functions and orderly mechanisms for adjustment among them. Worship of false unities produces conflict where discrete governance or dispute-resolution could operate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization concentrates power and produces absentee rulers
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect has been to concentrate decision in central governments, in distant executive offices ... The men who make the decisions at these central points are remote from the men they govern and the facts with which they deal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware policies that centralize decision-making over wide, complex affairs; remote decision-makers are prone to abstraction, legalism, and bureaucracy, and lack the local knowledge and consultation that gives rules legitimacy and fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules laid down at distance tend to lack consent and fit
rubrics_metrics.description: The more extensive the rule laid down the less account it can take of fact and special circumstance ... Distantly imposed rules usually lack the sanction of consent. Being less suited to the needs of men, and more external to their minds, they rest on force rather than on custom and on reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislation and regulation should be attentive to local particulars and consent mechanisms; otherwise enforcement will rely on coercion and encounter evasion or passive obedience rather than genuine compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public opinion's disciplining role weakens with absentee government
rubrics_metrics.description: The widening distance between the centers where decisions are taken and the places where the main work of the world is done has undermined the discipline of public opinion upon which all the earlier theorists relied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of democratic health should consider whether publics can form judgments based on accessible facts and timely feedback; long causal intervals and remote conditioning factors degrade the public's corrective capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: For complex national/international/industrial problems prefer many detailed balances over wholesale central control
rubrics_metrics.description: The pluralist ... would say that in place of vast wholesale balances of power it is necessary to create many detailed balances of power. The reduction of capitalism to workable law is no matter of striking at it wholesale by general enactments. It is a matter of defeating its arbitrary power in detail ... in every factory, in every office, in every market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tackle arbitrary power by building local and sectoral counterweights and rules—trade associations, local institutions, factory- or market-level regulation—rather than only by sweeping nationalizations or central laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish the roles and methods of actors vs. publics
rubrics_metrics.description: I have supposed that the opinions of the spectators must be essentially different from those of the actors, and that the kind of action they were capable of taking was essentially different too ... the public had a function and must have methods of its own in controversies, qualitatively different from those of the executive men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design civic processes acknowledging that the public (interested spectators) provides different judgments and interventions than executors of policy. Public action aims to promote conditions enabling special purposes to be reconciled, not to execute policy directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability requires breaking the fiction that private quarrels equal national quarrels
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary to break down the fiction of identity, to insist that the quarrel of one business man with another is their quarrel, and not the nation's ... If these essentially private disputes could be handled, without patriotic fervor ... the balance of power between governments would be easier to maintain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International and intergovernmental stability depends on treating many disputes as private/commercial and creating impartial adjudication mechanisms, avoiding conversion of private interests into national causes that escalate tensions.
